title: Negative information questions with singular action verbs
focus: Use the question word, the appropriate negative verb and the main verb's negative form: Miksi sinä et tule? Miksi sinä et tule? — Koska olen sairas.
targetSkills: Negative information questions with singular action verbs
prerequisiteSkills: Negative information questions with plural olla forms

exercises.prompt: Choose the question meaning “Why aren't you coming?”  Address one person (sinä).
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. Use the question word, the appropriate negative verb and the main verb's negative form: Miksi sinä et tule? (“Why aren't you coming?”). Form these negative main-verb forms by removing -n from the supplied I-form: tulen → tule, juon → juo, luen → lue. The negative form keeps the stem changes already present in the I-form. The complete question means “Why aren't you coming”.
requiredSkills: Negative information questions with singular action verbs
exercises.targetSkill: Negative information questions with singular action verbs

exercises.prompt: Answer “Mitä sinä et juo?”: choose “I do not drink coffee.”
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. A pronoun stands in place of a name or noun. Negative action objects use the partitive in these examples. The complete noun forms are supplied because object formation is not this lesson's target. The complete reply means “I do not drink coffee”.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: subject (who or what this sentence is about) + negative verb (marks not and identifies the person) + main verb after the negative verb + object (the thing the action concerns)

parts.role: subject (who or what this sentence is about)
parts.formation: Minä is the singular first-person subject pronoun, used by a speaker about themself.

parts.role: negative verb (marks not and identifies the person)
parts.formation: En is the first-person singular negative verb. The main verb takes its negative form.

parts.role: main verb after the negative verb
parts.formation: Juoda removes -da to form juo. This is the singular third-person affirmative form and, after a negative verb, the negative main-verb form; the long vowel does not lengthen further.

parts.role: object (the thing the action concerns)
parts.formation: Kahvi + -a gives kahvia, an unspecified amount of coffee.

parts.formation: Minä is the singular first-person subject pronoun, used by a speaker about themself.

parts.role: negative verb (marks not and identifies the person)
parts.formation: En is the first-person singular negative verb. The main verb takes its negative form.

parts.role: main verb after the negative verb
parts.formation: Remove -n from tulen to obtain the negative main-verb form tule; the negative verb carries the person.

parts.role: time
parts.formation: Huomenna is a complete time expression meaning tomorrow.

exercises.prompt: Repair “Hän en mene kouluun.” to mean “She is not going to school.” Use Hän (“he or she”), kouluun (“to school”), mennä (“to go”).
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. For a negative reply, change the addressed person's et into your en and keep the main verb's negative form: En juo kahvia (“I do not drink coffee”). Negative action objects use the partitive in these examples. The complete noun forms are supplied because object formation is not this lesson's target. The complete reply means “She is not going to school”.
requiredSkills: Negative information questions with singular action verbs
exercises.targetSkill: Negative information questions with singular action verbs

sentenceExplanation.translation: She is not going to school.
sentenceExplanation.pattern: subject (who or what this sentence is about) + negative verb (marks not and identifies the person) + main verb after the negative verb + destination

parts.role: subject (who or what this sentence is about)
parts.formation: Hän refers to one other person without specifying gender.

parts.role: negative verb (marks not and identifies the person)
parts.formation: Ei is the singular third-person present negative verb.

parts.role: main verb after the negative verb
parts.formation: Remove -n from menen to obtain negative mene, unchanged after every present negative verb.

parts.role: destination
parts.formation: Repeat the final u of koulu and add n: koulu + u + n gives kouluun.

answerDiagnostics.explanation: Match the negative verb to its subject: minä en, hän ei, me emme, he eivät.
After the negative verb use the unchanged negative stem, not an affirmative person form. Keep the negation when the meaning is negative.
